claims.statement: The Met dates the flourishing urban Indus civilization to approximately 2600–1900 BCE.
Harappa and Mohenjo Daro were large settlements connected with western trading partners.
Seals preserve writing that remains undeciphered.

evidence.locator: Timeline and Key Events: ca. 2600–1900 BCE
evidence.note: Broad source-level context. This does not establish activity in every year or reconstruct political borders. Approximate period boundaries follow this source.
